title: Why Your Wi-Fi Stutters When the Microwave Is On

beats.text: Your video freezes the second someone starts heating leftovers. That's not bad luck. Your Wi-Fi and your microwave have something weird in common, and it's floating around your kitchen right now.
Stop one: your router. It talks to your phone using invisible radio waves, and one of its main lanes is a band of the airwaves called 2.4 gigahertz.
Stop two: the kitchen. A microwave oven uses radio waves too, trapped inside a metal box. They make the water molecules in your food vibrate, and all that motion turns into heat.
Stop three: the door. The metal walls and that dotted screen keep nearly all of those waves inside the box, and federal safety rules strictly limit how much is allowed to leak.
Stop four: back at the router. While that oven is running, your phone and your router struggle to hear each other. That's the stall you see on your screen.

Here's the twist. Your microwave cooks at about 2.45 gigahertz, right inside the same band as that Wi-Fi lane. So the tiny bit that slips out works like a leaf blower starting up next to a quiet conversation. Harmless to you, but very loud to your Wi-Fi.

The fix? Many routers also have a 5 gigahertz lane the microwave doesn't touch. Or just move the router farther from the kitchen. Another one decoded. Does your Wi-Fi stutter when the microwave runs? Comment yes or no, and share this with whoever always blames the internet company. Next time your video freezes, check who's heating leftovers.

sources.claim: Wi-Fi commonly uses the 2.4 GHz band (and a 5 GHz band); microwave ovens emit in the 2.4 GHz band and can interfere with Wi-Fi
Home microwave ovens operate at about 2,450 MHz (2.45 GHz)
Microwaves make water molecules in food vibrate, producing heat; metal interior reflects the waves
Door screen holes are far smaller than the wavelength so microwaves stay in; a federal standard limits leakage (5 mW/cm2 at about 2 inches)
Leakage (not harmful to people, federally limited) can interfere with Wi-Fi/Bluetooth; moving to the 5 GHz band avoids it

fact_notes: CONFIRMED the plan's twist (same 2.4 GHz band). HEDGED: 'nearly all' waves stay inside; 'many routers' have 5 GHz. Worded as 'same band', not 'same frequency', and said Wi-Fi also uses another band. DROPPED: 'an old microwave is worse' from the plan (only one opened source says older units have poor shielding); power comparison (oven watts vs router watts) - not in an opened source; any health claim beyond 'federal rules strictly limit leakage' (FDA). No 'resonance' or 'cooks from the inside' wording. The leaf-blower line is the one analogy.
